about: The diagnostics of the library (E1(b), 2026-10-09): stdalign/diagnostics.py and stdalign/projection.py, against the library's tests and the checks of [P43]-[P51] and [P15].

mutants.name: [P44] named pursuit from the behaviour
edits: return project_linear(nearest_intended(p, q, F), A, A @ np.asarray(p, dtype=float))
return project_linear(np.asarray(p, dtype=float), A, A @ np.asarray(p, dtype=float))
mutants.note: Projecting from the default q instead of p° survived a first run, and is equivalent: F is a row of A, so tilt(p°, Aᵀθ) and tilt(q, Aᵀθ) range over the same family, and the I-projection onto {A·p = A·p̂} is unique ([P15](iii)); the two agree wherever both are defined (t* < ∞), to 5e-16 on 200 random instances. Projecting from the behaviour itself is not equivalent: it returns p̂, and nothing is left unexplained.
